cover.title: Think possibility, not probability
cover.body: AI can be a thought partner, not only a faster typist. Ask what you have not considered.
cover.example: Example: before you draft the bid memo, ask what the memo is missing.

confession.title: You get the average
confession.body: Ask for an answer and you get the middle of the curve. New options live at the edges.
confession.example: Example: ask for a vendor shortlist and you get the three everyone knows.

pulse.title: How often does AI show up in your week?
pulse.body: Answer on your phone and watch the room fill in. We ask again at the end.
pulse.example: Example: drafting with it is common. Deciding with it is a different step.

ladder.title: Possibility asks why we have farms
ladder.body: Probability makes the plow better. Possibility invents the tractor, then hydroponics.
ladder.example: Example: faster contract review is a better plow. Do we need this contract?

where.title: It's 2 a.m. and a resident has a question
where.body: Harbor, the agency's resident assistant, answers from the agency's own rules. A person reviews the work the next morning.
where.example: Example: a permit deadline question at midnight, checked by staff by breakfast.

system.title: Four moves, one real decision
system.body: Challenge, Invert, Multiply, Rehearse. Take one real decision through all four.
system.example: Example: one open purchase, tested from four sides.

move1.title: Question the assumption
move1.body: Every decision rests on something you believe. Say it out loud and test it.
move1.example: Example: does the RFP scope still match what residents need?

move2.title: Name the opposition
move2.body: Write the objection before someone else does. It shows you what you are missing.
move2.example: Example: draft the protest letter a losing bidder would send.

move3.title: Widen the range
move3.body: Two options is a choice between them. Add more, including the odd ones.
move3.example: Example: you have three bidders. Add a fourth, or no purchase at all.

move4.title: Rehearse the conversation you're dreading
move4.body: Pick the person you least want to talk to. Practice three exchanges, then ask what you missed.
move4.example: Example: a department director wants a bid waiver. Rehearse that meeting first.

principles.title: Four moves when you return to work
principles.body: Challenge, Invert, Multiply, Rehearse. The tool widens what you consider. The judgment stays yours.
principles.example: Example: does the cooperative contract scope match what we need?

movecheck.title: Which move will you try first?
movecheck.body: Pick one of the four and watch the room choose.
movecheck.example: Example: start with Challenge on the memo you send this week.

guardrails.title: Possibility is not permission
guardrails.body: Give it your values, check its work, keep sensitive data out, and ask IT when unsure.
guardrails.example: Example: no resident data goes in. Ask IT which tools are approved.

thisweek.title: Two questions before you commit
thisweek.body: What have we missed? What assumptions have we made? Ask an AI tool both about one real decision.
thisweek.example: Example: ask both of a scope before it goes up the chain.

pledge.title: How often does AI show up in your week?
pledge.body: Answer twice: Today, and where you expect to be in one month.
pledge.example: Example: a few times a month today, weekly in one month.

close.title: Expand your perspective, then decide
close.body: The tool widens what you consider. The judgment stays yours. Take it into a real conversation.
close.example: Example: more bidders on the table, and a person still signs.

walkout.title: Where we're going, we don't need roads
walkout.body: Thinking outside the box in the new world of AI.
walkout.example: Example: ask for the option nobody on the team has raised.
